theorem_title: Arithmetic semantics of the thirteen unlabelled YAH rows
natural_language_statement:
Let $R$ be the fixed list of thirteen unlabelled YAH instances, with full words $L_r$ and $R_r$ for each row $r$. Let $V$ evaluate a word from the initial value $1$, with digit maps $f:x\mapsto2x$, $t:x\mapsto2x+1$, and $j:x\mapsto3x+j$ for $j\in\{0,1,2\}$; boundary symbols leave the value unchanged. Define $S(n)=n/2$ for even $n$ and $S(n)=(3n+1)/2$ for odd $n$. Then

$$\forall r\in R,\qquad V(R_r)=\begin{cases}S(V(L_r)),&r\text{ uses a dynamic rule},\\ V(L_r),&r\text{ uses an auxiliary rule}.\end{cases}$$

Here the two dynamic rule names are $D_f,D_t$. The theorem checks the arithmetic meaning of these thirteen concrete instances; it does not quantify over all contexts.
